Which would be more rewarding: running an animal shelter or a nursing home?
Personally, I'd rather run a animal shelter.

Animal shelter. Sure, some of the animals have to be put down, but you can also save some. At a nursing home, they are all going to die there (or at a hospital right after leaving), and there's nothing you can do about it. It's just a matter of time. I've been to nursing homes, and even though the places I visited were good, well run establishments where the patients were treated well, it was still one of the most depressing places I've ever been.

Animal shelter.

But a more difficult question would be: which would be more rewarding: running an animal shelter or an orphanage?
So what do you think? Animals or orphans?

I'd pick an animal shelter. The condition of orphanages around the world is so deplorable right now. Even when the people who work in them care, there aren't enough resources to give the kids a decent start. With pets at least they only live a decade or two. Some of these kids are set up for 70 years of mental, physical, and social issues from the deprivation.
I run the orphanage. One person that really cares in a kids life can be huge to them. I'd be able to try to be that guy.

One of the benefits of working with animals is they forgive the past and appreciate even your smallest effort to help them. While I've known some wonderful people at the end of their lives, many are suffering from unwanted changes to their bodies, their surroundings, their schedules, and their independence. They can be angry, resentful, unstable and hurtful! The worst a cat can do is bite.

Combine the two, disadvantaged animals get love and company, the elderly have a companion they can "look after".

That would be most rewarding.
